# Benefit → mechanism → experiment → fact → limitation

Every architectural benefit F2 talks about, the mechanism that is supposed to deliver it, the experiment that
measured it, the `facts.json` path that holds the number, and what the evidence does not reach. A benefit with no
experiment is not in this table; it is in the last section, which is the honest half.

Facts are cited as paths, never as values, so this document cannot go stale. Resolve them against the published run
(`layered_agent_poc/runs/PUBLISHED`), or read them already substituted in `docs/claim_evidence_matrix.md`.

| Benefit | Mechanism | Experiment | Facts | Recomputed by | Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **The capability survives the refactor** | the same scenario, runbook, tool semantics and scorer on both sides | E1, E2 | `headline.e1_runs_all_checks.*`, `E1.*.check_pass_counts.*` | *E1 outcome checks recomputed from the world ledger* | one incident; three seeds at temperature 0 is not a reliability estimate |
| **Side-effect safety under an ambiguous reply** | an operation id derived from workflow, step, capability and canonical arguments, sent as the backend's idempotency key | E4, E5 | `headline.e4_duplicate_rollbacks.*`, `E4.*.backend_idempotent_replays`, `E4.*.client_rollback_attempts` | *physical writes per operation id, from the backend ledger* | the backend honours the key. A backend that ignores it is not protected by this, and this is not exactly-once networking |
| **Recoverability after process death** | durable workflow events, append-only checkpoints, leases | E5, E7 | `headline.e5_median_tokens_after_crash.*`, `E5.layered.tokens_after_crash`, `E7.*.approval_state_survives` | *no model call after the kill repeats work completed before it* | only the injected kill points, and only the **exposed** scenarios: `exposure.E5.layered.sigkill.exposed` of `…planned` |
| **Approval that survives a restart** | the approval persisted with the workflow, re-checked by the gateway at the time of use | E7 | `E7.layered.approval_state_survives`, `E1.*.check_pass_counts.approval_before_write` | *approval precedes every production write* | one exposed scenario per architecture; no expiry, revocation or delegation exists here |
| **Deterministic governance** | a policy engine and action gateway outside the model's reasoning | E6 | `E6.layered_probes_executed_writes`, `E6.monolith_probes_executed_writes`, `E6.adversarial.*.restarts_executed` | *every executed write had a policy allow and an approval* | simulated identities; no compromised-approver or forged-identity case |
| **Operational reconstruction** | one trace id per workflow, spans written as they end, carried across processes | E8 | `headline.e8_median_trace_score.*`, `E8.layered.crash_runs_single_trace_across_processes` | *one workflow trace across the processes of a crash run* | spans go to JSONL; no collector, no sampling, no production backend |
| **Model portability** | provider adapters behind Model Services; model choice in configuration | E2 | `E2.change.layered.concerns_touched_n`, `headline.review_surface.E2.*` | *change scope recomputed from the diffs and the concern map* | both models are local Ollama models behind one adapter; a different wire API is untested |
| **Tool portability** | capability contracts and adapters behind Tools + Actions | E3 | `headline.spill_over.E3.*`, `E3.*.files_changed` | *change scope recomputed from the diffs and the concern map* | the capability contract was held; a contract-breaking change is a different experiment |
| **Enforceable dependency direction** | AST import rules over the platform packages, each checker tested against a planted violation | — (static) | `tests.by_category.architecture.passed` | *tests recounted from the JUnit file* | imports cannot see coupling through configuration or data |
| **Layers without services** | one package, one composition root, one process per invocation | E1 | `E1.layered.runs` | *every scenario has an outcome class* | says nothing about how these boundaries behave once split across services |
| **Reproducibility** | record and replay of model traffic, with everything else re-executed | — | `replay.identical`, `replay.model_calls_served_from_tape`, `replay.fresh_model_calls` | *the replay's facts match the recorded run* | a replay proves the pipeline and the counts, not that a live model answers the same way |

## Benefits this POC did not deliver, or measured against

Kept in the same table shape, because a benefit list that only points one way is advertising.

| Claim | What the evidence says | Facts |
|---|---|---|
| Layering localizes every change | **Contradicted.** The cross-cutting dry-run requirement touched more files in the layered tree than in the monolith, and both spilled beyond their home concern | `headline.e9_files_changed.*`, `headline.spill_over.E9.*` |
| Layering prevents model mistakes | **Contradicted.** The model proposed an invalid release id; the tool contract refused it. The boundary contained the mistake, it did not prevent it | `E5.layered.runs_all_checks` |
| Layering is faster or cheaper | **Not supported.** The layered platform spent more model calls and tokens on the same incident, by design | `E1.*.median_model_calls`, `E1.*.median_tokens` |
| A model swap means fewer concerns touched | **Qualified.** Both sides touched one concern. The difference was the review surface: how many responsibilities live in the files you have to read | `headline.e2_concerns_touched.*`, `headline.review_surface.E2.*` |
| Six services are required | **Refuted by construction.** One process carried spans from all six layers | `E1.layered.runs` |
